To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
human vascular smooth muscle cells from restenosis sites demonstrate enhanced responses to p53, which may underlie the efficacy of brachy therapy and drug treatment for restenosis.
the p53 tumor suppress gene regulates growth arrest in response to DNA-damage in human vascular smooth muscle cells from restenosis or in-stent stenosis sites, but not in normal vessels.
the p53 tumor suppresser gene is inactive in vascular muscle cells (VMS) in angioplasty restinosis sites, promoting VMS accumulation and vessel stening.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of p53 in VSMC growth control.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of in-stent stenosis.
the role of p53 in the response to DNA damage of human vascular smooth muscle cells from restenosis sites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the success of bracotherapy for in-stent stenosis is due to an intact p53 response to DNA damage and that a restenosis-associated defect in cyclin degradation may underlie the failure of angioplasty to control in-stent restosis.

the p53 tumor suppresser gene is active in VSMCs from restenosis or in-stent stenosis sites and that this activity may be important for the response of these VSMCs to DNA-damaging agents such as radiation and cytotoxic drugs.
p53 is a key player in the regulation of cell proliferation and apoptosis of vascular smooth muscle cells from normal or restenosis sites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the p53 pathway is intact in r-VSMC but that the cyclin D degradation response to DNA damage is impaired in these cells.
p53 is active in r-VSMC and may underlie brachytherapy success.
the p53 tumor suppressors gene is active in r-VSMC but not n-VMSM and that this may contribute to the success of bracytherapy for in-stent stenosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
p53 function in human Vascular Smooth Muscle cells (VSMC) from normal vessels and from angioplasty restinosis/in-stent restinosis sites is normal or increased in the VSMCs from the restenosis sites.
p53 is not inactive in r-VSMC.

the p53 tumor suppresser is intact in human vascular smooth muscle cells derived from restenosis sites and is likely to play an important role in brachytherapy and in the effects of cytotoxic drug treatment for restenosis.
